title_en: Shanghai Dacheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. v. Lou Jianhua et al. — other company-related dispute
ruling_gist_en: 1. The articles of association are the fundamental rules for the organization and activities of a company. Where the articles of association of an asset appraisal company, as a special enterprise, stipulate that a shareholder must withdraw their shares upon retirement, and that the settlement month for such withdrawal shall be the month preceding the month of retirement, both the shareholder and the company shall perform in accordance with the articles of association when returning the shareholder's share of net assets in the company.

full_text_en:
Shanghai Dacheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. v. Lou Jianhua — dispute over other matters related to the company

Ruling Summary

1. A company's articles of association constitute the fundamental rules for the organization and activities of the company. Where the articles of association of an asset appraisal company, as a special type of enterprise, stipulate that a shareholder must withdraw from the company upon retirement, and that upon withdrawal, the settlement month shall be the month preceding the month of withdrawal, and the net asset share enjoyed by the shareholder in the company shall be refunded accordingly, the shareholder and the company shall perform in accordance with the articles of association.

2. The professional risk fund is a reserve set aside by accounting firms, asset appraisal institutions, and the like in accordance with regulations for the compensation of professional risks. According to the "Measures for the Administration of Professional Risk Funds of Asset Appraisal Institutions" (Cai Qi [2009] No. 26) issued by the Ministry of Finance, during the continuous operation of an asset appraisal institution, the balance of the professional risk fund shall be maintained at no less than 5% of the total appraisal business revenue of the preceding five years. On this premise, and subject to a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the partners' meeting, the accumulated professional risk fund that has been set aside for more than five years may be converted into distributable profits for the current year for distribution. Therefore, where a corresponding shareholders' meeting resolution of the asset appraisal company already exists, a request by a withdrawing shareholder for the distribution of the accumulated professional risk fund that has been set aside for more than five years may be upheld.

Plaintiff (Counterclaim Defendant): Shanghai Dacheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hengfeng Road, Zhabei District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Gu Meizhen, Chairperson of the Board of the company.

Defendant (Counterclaim Plaintiff): Lou Jianhua, female, 54 years old, Han Chinese, domiciled at Aomen Road, Putuo District, Shanghai.

Third Party: Shanghai Dacheng Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd., domiciled at Moling Road, Zhabei District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Liang Yong, Chairperson of the Board of the company.

Third Party: Shanghai Dacheng Financial Consulting Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hengfeng Road, Zhabei District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Gu Meizhen, Executive Director of the company.

The plaintiff, Shanghai Dacheng Asset Appraisal Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Asset Appraisal Company), filed an action with the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai against the defendant, Lou Jianhua, regarding other disputes related to the company.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff alleged that on January 27, 2005, the plaintiff's articles of association determined that the shareholders of the company were Gu Meizhen, the defendant Lou Jianhua, and four other persons, among whom the defendant held 16.66% of the shares, and stipulated that shareholders must withdraw their shares upon retirement and must withdraw their shares upon resignation. Subsequently, relevant documents stipulated that shareholders of asset appraisal institutions should hold a certificate of registered asset appraiser, but the defendant did not have such a certificate and had retired. On June 27, 2008, the plaintiff's shareholders' meeting resolved: (1) Order the defendant to withdraw her 16.66% shares in the plaintiff; (2) The defendant's 16.66% equity shares shall be transferred equally to the remaining shareholders of the plaintiff, including Gu Meizhen and four others, and the defendant's actual capital contribution of RMB 50,000 shall be paid by the five transferee shareholders to the plaintiff's finance office within three days after this resolution, and the plaintiff shall deliver the amount to the defendant before 12:00 noon on July 1, 2008, and handle the equity transfer procedures; (3) Based on the audit report on the plaintiff's financial condition for 2007, the plaintiff's net assets were negative and profits were negative for 2007, and the defendant is not entitled to any share of the plaintiff's net assets or any dividend distribution. After the shareholders' meeting resolution, the defendant refused to go through the share withdrawal procedures. Accordingly, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit. During the trial of this case, Items (2) and (3) of the above shareholders' meeting resolution of June 27, 2008, were revoked by an effective judgment, and, pursuant to an entrusted audit, the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, were RMB 912,940.29. With respect to the audit conclusion, the plaintiff argued that the revenues, costs, and expenses of the three companies (the plaintiff and the two Third Parties) were commingled. The audit included 80% of the revenue of the Third Party Consulting Company into the plaintiff's revenue. Although the corresponding labor service fees were transferred to the plaintiff's costs, only over RMB 70,000 was transferred for expenses, which was unreasonable. The plaintiff argued that expenses should be apportioned based on the revenue ratio (total business revenue of the three companies for 2006 and 2007: RMB 4,654,603; revenue of the two Third Parties: RMB 539,355; plaintiff's revenue ratio: 88.41%) for the following three items: 1. Year-end bonuses: RMB 111,799 distributed by the Third Party Consulting Company in 2006, and RMB 99,743 distributed by the plaintiff in 2007; the plaintiff's expenses should be increased by RMB 87,281 based on the revenue ratio apportionment. 2. Wages for 2006 and 2007: RMB 476,728.70 distributed by the plaintiff, RMB 142,825 distributed by the Third Party Real Estate Appraisal Company; the plaintiff's expenses should be increased by RMB 71,019 based on the revenue ratio apportionment. 3. Office rental expenses for 2006 and 2007: RMB 218,622.88 borne by the plaintiff, RMB 100,100 borne by the two Third Parties; the plaintiff's expenses should be increased by RMB 63,160 based on the revenue ratio apportionment. The total of the above three items results in an increase of RMB 221,460 in the plaintiff's expenses, and the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, should be reduced to RMB 691,480.29. Therefore, the plaintiff's claims are: 1. Confirm that the defendant ceased to be a shareholder of the plaintiff as of June 27, 2008; 2. Order the defendant to collect the withdrawal payment of RMB 115,200.62 from the plaintiff within 30 days from the effective date of this judgment, and meanwhile, the defendant shall withdraw her shares and assist in handling relevant industrial and commercial registration changes; 3. The litigation costs of this case shall be borne by the defendant.

The plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company submitted the following evidence in support of the main claim:
1. The June 27, 2008 shareholders' meeting resolution of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the defendant Lou Jianhua ceased to be a shareholder of the plaintiff as of June 27, 2008.
2. The January 27, 2005 articles of association of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that Articles 22 and 23 of the plaintiff's articles of association stipulate that shareholders who are unable to practice may retire and withdraw their shares, and specify the amount of the withdrawal payment.
3. The 2005 "Measures for the Administration of the Approval of Asset Appraisal Institutions", intended to prove that at that time, real estate appraisal and asset appraisal were required to be separated, and shareholders of asset appraisal institutions should hold a certificate of registered asset appraiser, but the defendant Lou Jianhua did not hold such a certificate.
4. Civil Judgment (2007) Zha Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 26, intended to prove that the defendant Lou Jianhua's labor contract expired on August 31, 2006, and the defendant left the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company on September 1, 2006.
5. Audit Report Shen Bei Hui Suo Cai Zi (2008) No. 76 (with financial statements and notes) dated February 2008, intended to prove that as of December 31, 2007, the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company had total assets of over RMB 790,000, a loss of RMB 290,000, and an investment of RMB 700,000 was not fully paid in, resulting in net assets of RMB -200,000.
6. The notice of issuance of the "Business License for Enterprise Legal Person" and the application for registration of establishment of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the plaintiff was registered and established with the Administration for Industry and Commerce in March 1996, with the nature of a collective enterprise and three legal persons as investors.
7. The 1998 application for change of registration of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the plaintiff was restructured from a collective enterprise into a limited liability company in 1998, at which time the shareholders were three legal persons and 7 employees (including the defendant Lou Jianhua).
8. The 2000 capital increase verification report and explanation of verification matters of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the three legal person shareholders withdrew, and the shareholders changed to 5 individuals, including the defendant Lou Jianhua.
9. The December 16, 1999 articles of association of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that Articles 22 and 23 of those articles of association regarding share withdrawal are consistent with the 2005 articles of association.
10. The May 31, 2008 balance sheet, income statement, and profit distribution statement of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that as of May 31, 2008, the plaintiff's net assets were RMB -830,000.
11. Arbitration Award Zha Lao Zhong (2006) Ban Zi No. 810, intended to prove that shareholders of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company must be current employees of the plaintiff, and that shareholders must withdraw their shares upon resignation.
12. The June 30, 2006 shareholders' meeting resolution of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the plaintiff's registered capital was actually paid in for a total of RMB 300,000, of which the defendant Lou Jianhua contributed RMB 50,000.
13. Civil Judgment (2008) Zha Min Er (Shang) Chu Zi No. 617, intended to prove that Item (1) of the June 27, 2008 shareholders' meeting resolution of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company was not revoked, but Items (2) and (3) were revoked.
14. The April 15, 2005 shareholders' meeting resolution of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the plaintiff and the two Third Parties operate as "three nameplates, one team".
15. The main tax payable schedules, income statements and profit distribution statements, transfer vouchers, year-end bonus calculation and distribution lists, the plaintiff's employee salary and bonus distribution management measures, payroll lists, lease contracts, renewal contracts, payment vouchers, and invoices for 2006 and 2007 relating to the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company and the two Third Parties, intended to prove that the plaintiff's net assets should be reduced by RMB 221,460.

Defendant's Defense (and Counterclaim): The defendant argued: First, the defendant agrees with the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company's first claim. Second, with respect to the plaintiff's second claim, the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, should be based on the audit conclusion, and should not be reduced as argued by the plaintiff. Therefore, the defendant's withdrawal payment should be 16.66% of the audited amount of RMB 912,940.29, which is RMB 152,095.85. The defendant has no objection to the remaining part of that claim. Third, according to the audit report in this case, as of May 31, 2008, the plaintiff's professional risk fund was RMB 2,162,070.59, of which RMB 1,231,898.49 was accumulated before June 30, 2004. According to the "Measures for the Administration of Professional Risk Funds of Asset Appraisal Institutions" (Cai Qi [2009] No. 26) and the "Memorandum on the Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf of Others" dated October 22, 2004, the contributors mentioned in the memorandum may enjoy the rights and interests relating to the period before June 30, 2004, in proportion to their contribution shares. The defendant held 10% of the shares before June 30, 2004, and is entitled to RMB 123,189.84 from the professional risk fund accumulated before June 30, 2004 (the defendant reserves the right to claim the professional risk fund accumulated after June 30, 2004). Accordingly, the defendant filed a counterclaim, seeking: 1. An order that the plaintiff pay the defendant a withdrawal payment of RMB 152,095.85; 2. An order that the plaintiff pay the defendant interest on the loss (calculated on the principal of RMB 152,095.85 from July 1, 2008, at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period, until the effective date of this judgment); 3. An order that the plaintiff refund to the defendant RMB 123,189.84 from the professional risk fund accumulated before June 30, 2004; 4. The litigation costs and appraisal fees of this case shall be borne by the plaintiff.

The defendant submitted the following evidence in support of the main claim and counterclaim:
1. Judicial Accounting Appraisal No. Hu Jin Shen Cai Zi [2007] No. F3625 dated February 2007, intended to prove the business scope of the Third Party Consulting Company and the investment status of shareholders in the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, and that the plaintiff's operating revenue and profits were transferred to the Third Party Consulting Company.
2. The July 21, 2003 shareholders' meeting resolution, meeting minutes, and loan note of the same date of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, intended to prove that the registered capital of RMB 500,000 was not contributed by Gu Meizhen herself.
3. The June 29, 2008 notice and the receipt for domestic registered mail of the following day, intended to prove that the defendant Lou Jianhua notified in writing the shareholders of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company that the shareholders who signed the plaintiff's shareholders' meeting resolution were not entitled to acquire the equity.
4. "Notice of the Ministry of Finance on Matters Concerning the Work during the Transition Period of Asset Appraisal Institutions" (Cai Qi [2008] No. 43), intended to prove that the transferees of the equity under the plaintiff's shareholders' meeting resolution were not entitled to acquire the equity.
5. The investigation letter dated August 15, 2008, issued by the Shanghai Social Insurance Fund Settlement and Management Center, intended to prove that Sun Yuemei, Liu Qiong, Ji Xinjun, and Shen Zhangrong, who signed the plaintiff's shareholders' meeting resolution, had left the plaintiff to work for other entities, and their pension insurance contributions were being made by those other entities.
6. The reply from the Shanghai Appraisal Association to the investigation order, intended to prove that Sun Yuemei, Liu Qiong, and Shen Zhangrong had transferred their practice to other firms and left the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company. Since resigned employees must withdraw their shares, they were not qualified to acquire the equity.
7. Audit Report Shen Bei Hui Suo Cai Zi (2008) No. 76 (with financial statements and notes) dated February 2008, intended to prove that the audit did not reflect long-term investments, and that items such as tax rewards recorded under other payables (liabilities) were incorrect and should be treated as profits.
8. "Measures for the Administration of Professional Risk Funds of Asset Appraisal Institutions" (Cai Qi [2009] No. 26), the "Memorandum on the Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf of Others" dated October 22, 2004, and the shareholders' meeting resolutions of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company dated October 21 and November 5, 2004, intended to prove that the professional risk fund should be distributed in accordance with the measures, and that the defendant Lou Jianhua was entitled to 10% of the rights and interests before June 30, 2004, and 16.66% thereafter.
9. Industrial and commercial registration archive materials of the Third Party Consulting Company, intended to prove that 55% of its equity originally belonged to the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company, and was later transferred to Gu Meizhen's name.
10. Information on the evaluation reports issued by the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company but for which revenue was recorded by the Third Party Consulting Company from January to July 2006 (amounting to over RMB 1.03 million in total), intended to prove that both the contracts and reports were issued by the plaintiff, but the appraisal fees were recorded in the Third Party Consulting Company's accounts, which affected the plaintiff's net asset value.

In response to the defendant Lou Jianhua's counterclaim, the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company argued: First, with respect to the defendant's counterclaim for the withdrawal payment, since the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, should be reduced to RMB 691,480.29, the defendant's withdrawal payment should be RMB 115,200.62. Second, with respect to the defendant's counterclaim for interest on the withdrawal payment, since the plaintiff's net assets were determined by the audit in this case, and there is no agreement or precedent for interest, no interest should be paid. Third, with respect to the defendant's counterclaim for the professional risk fund, the fund is intended to protect normal operations and is not part of shareholder equity; it cannot be refunded. Furthermore, the Ministry of Finance does not mandate its distribution, and this audit did not determine the fund either. Therefore, the defendant's counterclaim on this point is without merit. If distribution were to occur, an additional 25% corporate income tax would need to be paid.

The evidence submitted by the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company in response to the defendant Lou Jianhua's counterclaim was the same as that submitted for the main claim.

The Third Parties, the Real Estate Appraisal Company and the Consulting Company, stated that they agreed with the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company's position.

The Third Parties submitted the following evidence in support of the main claim and counterclaim:
1. The main tax payable schedules, income statements, and profit distribution statements of the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company and the two Third Parties for 2006 and 2007, intended to prove that the three companies operate as one team, and the arrangement was for tax benefits and operational convenience, with total combined business revenue of the three companies during the said years amounting to approximately RMB 4.65 million.
2. Three lease contracts and renewal contracts, intended to prove the payment status of rental expenses.
3. The plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company's employee salary and bonus distribution management measures, intended to prove the method of distributing labor service fees and bonuses.
4. The statistical table of labor service fee disbursement in November 2007, intended to prove that the judicial accounting appraisal opinion understated the labor service fees distributed by the Third Party Consulting Company by RMB 28,968.
5. The complete payroll lists of all wages paid by the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company and the Third Party Real Estate Appraisal Company in 2006 and 2007, intended to prove that the Third Party Real Estate Appraisal Company shouldered more of the payroll based on the revenue ratio apportionment of expenses.

During the trial of this case, the court examined the relevant provisions and, upon application of the parties, entrusted an audit.

Facts Found by the First Instance, Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai:

I. The plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company was registered and established upon approval by the Administration for Industry and Commerce on March 4, 1996. At its establishment, it was a collective enterprise with a registered capital of RMB 300,000. Subsequently, the plaintiff was restructured into a limited liability company. The current industrial and commercial registration records show that the plaintiff has a registered capital of RMB 1,000,000, with shareholders being Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, and the defendant Lou Jianhua (with capital contributions of RMB 750,000, RMB 25,000, RMB 105,000, and RMB 120,000, respectively), and Gu Meizhen is the legal representative.

II. On December 16, 1999, five individuals, namely Gu Meizhen, Ji Xinjun, Sun Yuemei, Wan Jianhua, and the defendant Lou Jianhua, as shareholders of the plaintiff, signed the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company's articles of association (hereinafter referred to as the 1999 Articles of Association, which were filed with the Administration for Industry and Commerce). These articles of association stipulated that the plaintiff's registered capital was RMB 300,000, with the defendant's contribution being RMB 70,000. Furthermore, in these articles: (1) Article 13 stipulated that shareholders of the plaintiff must meet the conditions of being a registered asset appraiser or having similar professional qualifications. (2) Article 20 stipulated that a shareholder intending to transfer capital contributions or withdraw shares shall submit a written application three months in advance, which shall be considered and approved by the board of directors and subject to the written consent of shareholders representing two-thirds of the capital contributions at the shareholders' meeting. (3) Article 21 stipulated that if a person loses the qualification of a shareholder due to the revocation of the certificate of registered asset appraiser or similar professional qualifications, upon consideration and approval by the board of directors and a report to the shareholders' meeting for the written consent of shareholders representing two-thirds of the capital contributions, a resolution may be passed to expel such person, and the shareholders' meeting shall decide on and dispose of such person's shareholder rights and interests. (4) Article 22 stipulated that if a shareholder is unable to practice due to age or health reasons, upon consideration by the board of directors and approval by a vote of the shareholders' meeting, the shareholder may retire, and must withdraw shares upon retirement. (5) Article 23 stipulated that when a shareholder withdraws shares, the settlement month shall be the month preceding the month of withdrawal, and the net asset share enjoyed by the shareholder in the plaintiff shall be refunded. If the plaintiff has difficulty refunding the amount in one lump sum, it may be refunded in installments, but not exceeding one year, and interest shall be paid from the date of withdrawal to the date of actual payment, calculated by reference to the same-period interest rate of the People's Bank of China. (6) Article 42 stipulated that the plaintiff shall set aside 10% of its business revenue for the professional risk fund and the enterprise development fund.

Subsequently, up to September 2006, the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company filed several amendments to the articles of association concerning registered capital, shareholders, and their capital contributions with the Administration for Industry and Commerce.

III. On October 21 and 22, 2004, five individuals including Dai Ye, Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, and the defendant Lou Jianhua signed the "Memorandum on the Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf of Others". This memorandum stipulated: (1) As of June 30, 2004, the plaintiff Asset Appraisal Company's actually paid-in capital was RMB 300,000, of which Gu Meizhen contributed RMB 60,000, the defendant RMB 30,000, Shen Zhangrong RMB 25,000, Ji Xinjun RMB 35,000, and the five individuals including Dai Ye (respectively held under the names of Gu Meizhen, the defendant, and Ji Xinjun) RMB 150,000; (2) To resolve the legacy issues of shareholding on behalf of others, the five individuals including Dai Ye would withdraw their shares in the amount of their contributions, and the net asset value of the plaintiff as of June 30, 2004, after adjustments based on the accounting statements, would be distributed to the original contributors. Among the adjustment items, there was an additional provision for the under-provision of the professional risk fund for the years 2000 to 2002 in the amount of RMB 363,050.19, reducing the distributable profits by RMB 363,050.19; (3) If the plaintiff undergoes liquidation events (including the professional risk fund) such as merger or dissolution within five years (before June 30, 2009), or if the relevant authorities issue new regulations on the provision and disposal of the professional risk fund, the contributors mentioned in this memorandum may enjoy the rights and interests relating to the period before June 30, 2004, in proportion to their contribution shares, and bear the same proportion of risk.

During the trial of this case, the plaintiff and the defendant confirmed: the plaintiff's occupational risk fund has been accrued at 10% of business revenue; the content of item (3) of the above memorandum regarding the occupational risk fund was agreed upon because the fund was not distributable under the then-prevailing regulations; before 2005, the plaintiff was subject to tax withholding on behalf of the tax authorities. The plaintiff confirmed: the plaintiff has not been operating since June 30, 2008, when it ceased to issue appraisal reports.

On October 21, 2004, and November 5, 2004, Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, and the defendant Lou Jianhua each signed a shareholder resolution of the plaintiff's assets appraisal company. The resolution dated October 21, 2004, stated: "All shareholders have discussed, revised, and finalized the formal version of the Memorandum on Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf, and it shall be implemented in accordance with the memorandum." The resolution dated November 5, 2004, stated: "The capital contributions withdrawn by the persons holding shares on behalf of others shall be subscribed by the defendant and five others, with the subscription date commencing July 1, 2004, of which the defendant contributed RMB 20,000."

4. On January 27, 2005, Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, Sun Yuemei, Liu Qiong, and the defendant Lou Jianhua, as shareholders of the plaintiff, signed a new articles of association of the plaintiff's assets appraisal company (hereinafter referred to as the 2005 Articles, not filed with the Administration for Industry and Commerce). The articles provided that the plaintiff's registered capital was RMB 1,000,000, of which the defendant contributed RMB 166,600, representing 16.66%. Additionally, Articles 13, 20, 21, 23, and 42 of the 2005 Articles were substantially consistent with the corresponding provisions of the 1999 Articles. Article 22 of the 2005 Articles, in addition to incorporating the content of Article 22 of the 1999 Articles, added that shareholders must withdraw their shares upon resignation.

5. On September 1, 2006, the defendant Lou Jianhua left the plaintiff's assets appraisal company. On February 5, 2007, this court, on the grounds that the labor contract between the plaintiff and the defendant expired on August 31, 2006, and the defendant explicitly declined to renew it, rendered a judgment in the labor contract dispute case [(2007) Zha Min Yi (Min) Chu Zi No. 26] dismissing the defendant's claim for reinstatement of the labor relationship with the plaintiff. The defendant confirmed that he officially retired in February 2008.

6. On June 27, 2008, the plaintiff's assets appraisal company held a shareholders' meeting and passed the following resolutions by vote: (1) In accordance with Article 22 of the plaintiff's 1999 and 2005 Articles of Association, the provisions of the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Construction requiring the separation of assets appraisal and real estate appraisal operations, and the fact that the defendant Lou Jianhua had left the plaintiff and was no longer an employee of the plaintiff, it was resolved to order the defendant to withdraw his 16.66% shares in the plaintiff; (2) The defendant's 16.66% equity interest was to be transferred equally to the remaining shareholders, namely Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, Sun Yuemei, and Liu Qiong. The defendant's actual capital contribution of RMB 50,000 was to be paid by the five transferee shareholders to the plaintiff's finance office within three days of this resolution, and the plaintiff was to deliver the amount to the defendant before 12:00 p.m. on July 1, 2008, and handle the equity transfer procedures; (3) Based on the audit report on the plaintiff's financial condition for 2007 issued in February 2008, the plaintiff's net assets for 2007 were negative, and profits were negative; therefore, the defendant was not entitled to any share of the plaintiff's net assets or to receive any dividends [Item (3) of the resolution supplemented Item (2) above]. All shareholders of the plaintiff except the defendant agreed to the above resolutions.

The audit report of February 2008 [i.e., Shen Bei Hui Suo Cai Zi (2008) No. 76], attached to the plaintiff's 2007 financial statements, noted that as of the end of 2007, the plaintiff's total assets were over RMB 3.06 million, total liabilities were over RMB 2.26 million, and net assets were over RMB 790,000. The plaintiff's balance sheet as of May 31, 2008, showed total assets of over RMB 2.83 million and total liabilities of over RMB 2.30 million.

On August 25, 2008, the defendant Lou Jianhua sued the plaintiff's assets appraisal company in this case, seeking to have the shareholders' resolution of June 27, 2008, set aside. During the trial of that case, the plaintiff affirmed the 2005 Articles of Association. The defendant, Gu Meizhen, Shen Zhangrong, Ji Xinjun, Sun Yuemei, and Liu Qiong all confirmed that the plaintiff's articles of association and the shareholders' shareholding ratios should be based on the 2005 Articles. On February 27, 2009, the court rendered a judgment setting aside Items (2) and (3) of the plaintiff's shareholders' resolution of June 27, 2008 (this judgment has become effective).

7. During the trial of this case, regarding the plaintiff's net asset value as of May 31, 2008, the plaintiff originally claimed it was negative RMB 830,000, while the defendant Lou Jianhua originally claimed it was RMB 790,000 and requested adjustments for the plaintiff's long-term investment representing a 55% stake in the third-party consulting company and for the plaintiff's transfer of appraisal income of over RMB 1.03 million to the third-party consulting company, among other matters. The court, upon the defendant's application, commissioned Qiu Shi Accounting Firm to audit the plaintiff's net asset value as of May 31, 2008, and upon the plaintiff's application, to audit the recording of the plaintiff's income, costs, and expenses in the accounts of the two third parties (and accordingly adjust the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008). On September 2, 2009, Qiu Shi issued Judicial Accounting Expert Opinion No. 9 [Hu Qiu Hui Ye (2009) Jian Zi No. 9], which concluded that after audit adjustments, as of May 31, 2008, the plaintiff's total assets were RMB 3,163,509.26, total liabilities were RMB 2,221,600.97, and owner's equity (net assets) totaled RMB 941,908.29. The opinion stated: (1) The third-party consulting company paid the plaintiff's costs (service fees) of RMB 835,094.96, which was treated as a reduction of profit in the audit; (2) The adjusted paid-in capital balance of the plaintiff was RMB 300,000, of which the defendant actually contributed RMB 50,000; (3) The occupational risk fund was adjusted upward due to the increase in main business income; after adjustment, other long-term liabilities, i.e., the occupational risk fund, amounted to RMB 2,162,070.59, of which RMB 1,231,898.49 was before June 30, 2004. On September 22, 2009, Qiu Shi issued a supplementary opinion, stating that on September 17, 2009, Gu Meizhen pointed out that in the original opinion, the costs (service fees) paid by the third-party consulting company to the plaintiff of RMB 835,094.96 were understated by RMB 28,968; after adjustment, the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, were RMB 912,940.29.

The above facts are evidenced by the civil judgment, articles of association, the Memorandum on Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf, relevant documents, shareholders' resolutions, the judicial accounting expert opinion and its supplementary opinion, transcripts of interviews, and trial transcripts.

The Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai held at first instance as follows:

The proportion of shares held by the defendant Lou Jianhua in the plaintiff's assets appraisal company should be his actual shareholding ratio of 16.66%. He had already retired. The plaintiff's articles of association provided that shareholders must withdraw their shares upon retirement. Item (1) of the shareholders' resolution of June 27, 2008, passed by the plaintiff's meeting in accordance with the articles of association, requiring the defendant to withdraw his 16.66% shares in the plaintiff, had not been set aside by a judgment and should be effective. On the date that resolution was passed, the defendant lost his status as a shareholder. The defendant now also agrees with this. The court supports the plaintiff's claims in the main action that do not involve specific amounts of withdrawal consideration, such as the confirmation that the defendant ceased to be a shareholder of the plaintiff from June 27, 2008. Regarding the specific amount of withdrawal consideration, interest on the withdrawal consideration, and the issue of the occupational risk fund, which are disputed in the main and counterclaims, the court is of the opinion:

First, concerning the specific amount of withdrawal consideration. Items (2) and (3) of the shareholders' resolution of June 27, 2008, of the plaintiff's assets appraisal company, which involved the specific amount, have been set aside by an effective judgment of the court. According to the plaintiff's articles of association, when a shareholder withdraws, the settlement month is the month preceding the month of withdrawal, and the shareholder is entitled to the refund of his share of the plaintiff's net assets as of that settlement month. Since the defendant Lou Jianhua ceased to be a shareholder of the plaintiff from June 27, 2008, the settlement month should be May 2008 for this case, and the defendant's 16.66% share of the plaintiff's net assets should be refunded. There is no dispute among the parties on this point. The audit conclusion now is that the plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, were RMB 912,940.29. The defendant confirms this. However, the plaintiff argues that because the income, costs, and expenses of the plaintiff and the two third parties were intermingled, the plaintiff should further allocate year-end bonuses, wages, and office expenses totaling RMB 221,460 in proportion to income, reducing net assets to RMB 691,480.29. The court is of the opinion that if the plaintiff's argument were accepted, all expenses would have to be allocated proportionally, but such allocation would result in the equalization of profits among the plaintiff and the two third parties. The plaintiff is an assets appraisal company, while the two third parties are a consulting company and a real estate appraisal company, respectively. The business fields of the three companies are not identical, and their actual incomes should not be the same. Moreover, based on the income ratios calculated by the plaintiff itself, the incomes of the two third parties were low, making profit equalization unreasonable. The plaintiff's above argument lacks sufficient basis and is not accepted. The plaintiff's net assets as of May 31, 2008, were RMB 912,940.29, and at the defendant's shareholding ratio of 16.66%, the plaintiff should pay the defendant withdrawal consideration of RMB 152,095.85. The court supports the defendant's corresponding counterclaim (the plaintiff's related claim in the main action is included herein).

Second, concerning interest on the withdrawal consideration. According to the plaintiff's assets appraisal company's articles of association, if the plaintiff has difficulty in refunding the withdrawal consideration in a lump sum, it may do so in installments, but not exceeding one year, and shall pay interest at the benchmark interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period from the date of withdrawal to the date of actual payment. Since the defendant Lou Jianhua ceased to be a shareholder of the plaintiff from June 27, 2008, the plaintiff should have paid the defendant the withdrawal consideration at that time. However, the plaintiff failed to pay the amount. Therefore, in accordance with the articles of association, the plaintiff should pay interest from that date. The court supports the defendant's counterclaim for interest on the withdrawal consideration calculated from July 1, 2008.

Third, concerning the occupational risk fund. The defendant Lou Jianhua reserves the right to claim for the occupational risk fund after June 30, 2004. Regarding the occupational risk fund before June 30, 2004, which is the subject of the defendant's counterclaim in this case, the Memorandum on Withdrawal of Shares Held on Behalf dated October 22, 2004, stipulated that if the plaintiff's assets appraisal company undergoes liquidation events (including the occupational risk fund) such as merger or cessation of business within five years (before June 30, 2009), or if there are new regulations from higher authorities regarding the accrual or disposal of the occupational risk fund, the contributors covered by this memorandum may enjoy the rights to the fund accumulated before June 30, 2004, in proportion to their capital contributions and bear the same proportion of risk. The parties now confirm that the above provisions regarding the occupational risk fund were made because the fund was not distributable under the then-prevailing regulations. Therefore, if the current regulations permit distribution and the distribution conditions are met, distribution should be made in accordance with the memorandum. Given that the Ministry of Finance's Document Cai Qi [2009] No. 26, the "Measures for the Administration of Occupational Risk Funds of Assets Appraisal Institutions," promulgated in February 2009, provides that, subject to ensuring the required balance, the portion of the occupational risk fund that has been accrued for more than five years and remains may be transferred to distributable profits for the current year upon a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or the partners, and given that the plaintiff's shareholders' meeting on October 21, 2004, resolved to implement the memorandum, the plaintiff's occupational risk fund accumulated before June 30, 2004, now meets the distribution conditions and is distributable. According to the audit, the plaintiff's risk fund before June 30, 2004, was RMB 1,231,898.49. The memorandum in question explicitly states that the defendant held 10% of the shares before June 30, 2004, meaning the plaintiff should pay the defendant 10% of this amount, i.e., RMB 123,189.84. The defendant's counterclaim for the occupational risk fund before June 30, 2004, should be supported. As for the plaintiff's argument regarding the corporate income tax on the occupational risk fund before June 30, 2004, according to the "Measures for Deduction Before Corporate Income Tax," the occupational risk fund should be deducted after tax, and the plaintiff was subject to tax withholding on behalf of the tax authorities before 2005, meaning the relevant corporate income tax had already been withheld in full based on the income amount. However, if tax is actually required to be paid in the future, the plaintiff may separately claim against the defendant based on the actual tax rate and method of payment. Additionally, the total audit fees for this case are RMB 120,000. Considering the original claims of the plaintiff and the defendant, as well as the significant discrepancy between the financial statements submitted by the plaintiff and the audit conclusion, the court determines that the plaintiff shall bear RMB 96,000 and the defendant shall bear RMB 24,000.

Accordingly, on October 23, 2009, the Zhabei District People's Court of Shanghai rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant Lou Jianhua shall cease to be a shareholder of the plaintiff Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. from June 27, 2008;

2. The plaintiff Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Lou Jianhua withdrawal consideration of RMB 152,095.85 within ten days of this judgment taking effect;

3. The plaintiff Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Lou Jianhua interest losses (calculated on the base amount of RMB 152,095.85 at the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period from July 1, 2008, to the date this judgment takes effect) within ten days of this judgment taking effect;

4. The defendant Lou Jianhua shall complete the withdrawal of his 16.66% equity interest in the plaintiff Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. and assist with the relevant industrial and commercial registration changes within thirty days of this judgment taking effect;

5. The plaintiff Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd. shall pay the defendant Lou Jianhua RMB 123,189.84 for the occupational risk fund accumulated before June 30, 2004, within ten days of this judgment taking effect.

The Assets Appraisal Company, dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, alleging: The Judicial Accounting Expert Opinion No. 9 [Hu Qiu Hui Ye (2009) Jian Zi No. 9] violated the principle of matching income with costs and expenses, failing to make corresponding adjustments for the intermingled income, costs, and expenses of the appellant and the original third parties, Dacheng Financial Consulting Company and Dacheng Real Estate Appraisal Company, resulting in an inflated net asset value of the appellant as of May 31, 2008; moreover, regarding employee travel expenses of over RMB 110,000, according to the Ministry of Finance's Document Cai Qi [2009] No. 242, promulgated and effective in November 2009, these cannot be offset against welfare expenses, and the undistributed profits of RMB 150,000 have not been reduced by income tax, both of which should be adjusted in the net asset value; regarding the calculation of interest on the withdrawal consideration, since there was a dispute over whether the withdrawal should occur, the appellant did not intentionally delay, and thus no interest should be paid, and even if interest is payable, it should be calculated at the deposit rate in accordance with the appellant's corporate practice; according to the Ministry of Finance's 2009 regulations, the distribution of the occupational risk fund must be decided by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, and the appellant's 2004 shareholders' resolution did not explicitly provide for the distribution of the occupational risk fund, so it should not be distributed, and even if it is to be distributed, it should be after deducting taxes. Therefore, the appellant requested that Items 2, 3, and 5 of the first instance judgment be set aside and amended accordingly.

The appellee Lou Jianhua responded: The Judicial Accounting Expert Opinion No. 9 is lawful and well-founded, and the appellee agrees with its conclusions; the failure to pay the withdrawal consideration in a timely manner was caused by the appellant's provision of false financial reports, and the appellant was at fault, so interest should be paid in accordance with the relevant legal provisions; in 2004, the shareholders of the appellant had already reached a consensus on the distribution of the occupational risk fund, and that resolution remains effective. Combined with the relevant provisions of the Ministry of Finance in 2009, the appellee's entitlement to the distribution of the occupational risk fund is well-founded, and the appellant's current shareholders have no right to dispose of or profit from the 2004 income. The appellee disagrees with the appellant's grounds of appeal.

The original third party, Dacheng Financial Consulting Company, stated that it agreed with the appellant's submissions on appeal.

The original third party, Dacheng Real Estate Appraisal Company, did not express any opinion.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The issues in dispute in this second instance were: 1. The determination of the net asset value of the appellant, the Assets Appraisal Company, as of May 31, 2008; 2. Whether interest on the withdrawal consideration should be paid, and if so, at what rate; 3. Whether the occupational risk fund should be paid, and if so, how.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held at second instance:

All parties in this case agree that the appellee Lou Jianhua ceased to be a shareholder of the appellant, the Assets Appraisal Company, from June 27, 2008. The court confirms this. Regarding the first issue in dispute, the appellant's net assets as of May 31, 2008, have been determined by Judicial Accounting Expert Opinion No. 9 [Hu Qiu Hui Ye (2009) Jian Zi No. 9]. The appellant's claim that the costs of the two original third parties should be allocated to it lacks factual basis and does not comply with relevant accounting standards. Moreover, Qiu Shi had already made corresponding adjustments based on the audit materials. Therefore, the court does not support the appellant's argument on this point. The appellant argues that, according to the Ministry of Finance's regulations, the employee travel expenses of over RMB 110,000 cannot be offset against welfare expenses. However, this regulation was promulgated and implemented in November 2009, and its effect does not retroactively apply to the time the expenses were incurred and the judicial accounting expert opinion was issued. The court does not accept this argument as credible. Regarding the RMB 150,000 in undistributed profits and the failure to withhold taxes, the appellant has not paid the relevant taxes and has not yet received a tax payment notice. Therefore, it is impossible to determine whether tax should be paid on the RMB 150,000 and the taxable amount. The judicial accounting expert opinion's failure to deduct the relevant taxes from the appellant's net assets is not improper. If the appellant actually incurs tax expenses in the future, it may pursue a separate claim. Regarding the second issue in dispute, according to the appellant's articles of association and the shareholders' resolution of June 27, 2008, the appellee's withdrawal of shares was clear. The parties only disputed the calculation of the withdrawal consideration amount. However, the shareholders' resolution passed by the appellant regarding the calculation of the appellee's withdrawal consideration has been set aside by an effective judgment of the court. Therefore, the appellant's failure to pay the withdrawal consideration in full and on time in accordance with the regulations was improper. The appellant should pay the corresponding interest in accordance with the articles of association. As for the interest rate standard, the appellant's claim that it should be based on the bank's deposit rate for the corresponding period lacks factual basis, and the court does not accept it. Regarding the third issue in dispute, the appellant's 2004 shareholders' resolution clearly stated that if higher authorities issue new regulations on the disposal of the occupational risk fund, the relevant contributors may enjoy the rights to the fund accumulated before June 30, 2004, in proportion to their capital contributions. Therefore, the appellant's shareholders' meeting had already passed a resolution on the distribution of the occupational risk fund, satisfying the distribution conditions set out in the Ministry of Finance's Document Cai Qi [2009] No. 26, and distribution is permissible. As for the appellant's argument that the occupational risk fund should first be subject to taxation, the first instance judgment has already provided a full explanation, and the court will not repeat it here. In summary, the facts found at first instance were clear, and the judgment was not improper. The appellant's grounds of appeal lack factual and legal basis.

Accordingly, on February 26, 2010, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court, in accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The appeal fee of RMB 5,589.28 shall be borne by the appellant, Shanghai Dacheng Assets Appraisal Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
